title: Gib and Spindleshanks' Lost Blanket
markdown:
Once, in the Twinkletop Hills beneath the tallest kindest mountains, where moonlight liked to stay, Gib lived in a cozy round burrow among whispering ferns. He was a very small goblin, moss-rain eyes, little green ears that wiggled when he was curious, which was often. Inside: warm damp earth after drizzle, berry tea on a stone stove, walls lined with smooth cool pebbles that sparkled in the soft light.

One sleepy morning sunbeams like pale yellow ribbons peeked through the round window and painted golden stripes on the mossy floor. Gib yawned a wide happy yawn, toes curling, ears wiggling. Then a tiny worry, dewdrop-small, landed in his tummy. Spindleshanks, his dearest hedgehog, was stirring. The quills were not prickly; they were dandelion-fluff soft. He always slept with his favourite blanket: very woolly, twilight purple, smelling of starlight and warm milk and cozy-dream whispers. Today Spindleshanks looked around with a sad frown, nose twitching. The blanket was nowhere.

“Oh, Spindleshanks. Your blanket is missing.” Gib’s heart felt a pebble too deep in a pocket. He would not let his friend be without comfort. He scooped the hedgehog up, warm, a gentle tickle of quills. “We will find it. A gentle adventure.”

So, with Spindleshanks nestled safely in his arms, soft quills tucked near Gib’s ear, Gib stepped out of his cozy burrow into the warm lantern wood. The trees were tall and friendly, branches reaching like welcoming arms, dappled with sunlight. Little lanterns of captured fireflies blinked along the winding path. The air was warm and smelled of sweet wild blossoms and something comforting and earthy, like freshly baked bread.

As they walked, Gib hummed a little goblin tune that floated like a dandelion seed. Spindleshanks made soft happy sounds against his shoulder, bubbles popping in warm milk. They looked under big friendly toadstools wide enough to be umbrellas, and peeked behind mossy logs that looked like sleepy green giants. “Is it here?” Gib would whisper, breath warm on the quills, and Spindleshanks would shake his head, tiny ears twitching. They explored by a gentle stream that sang over smooth stones, and among patches of soft velvet moss.

Around a bend where lanterns glowed brighter: a pretty cottage, mossy tiles, chimney puffing flower-calm smoke. By a bubbling stream a kind-faced witch in a long woolly rosy-pink dress, the warmest fluffiest honey-coloured mittens Gib had ever seen, two little clouds.

“Hello, little ones. What brings you wandering, with such a thoughtful friend in your arms?”

Gib, shy and happy, held Spindleshanks closer. “We are looking for his blanket. Very soft. Smells like home. Not in the burrow.”

She smiled, crinkly, eyes like lanterns. “An important thing, a blanket that holds comfort.” She wiggled the mittens. “When did he last have it? Where does he love to feel most snuggly? Where does he curl for his sweetest dreams?”

Gib furrowed. Spindleshanks squeaked as if agreeing. Memory: curling by the warmest part of the hearth, embers like sleepy stars, nudging the blanket under his chin with his nose, quills relaxing when tucked just so.

“The hearth! That’s his favourite cozy spot!”

“The best adventures lead us right back to where we started.”

Gib thanked her, waved, hurried home with the hedgehog snuggled closer. Lanterns winked. He did not need the trees to guess for him.

As Gib pushed open the door, warm air and the smell of home came to him. And there, right by the gentle welcoming glow of the embers, was Spindleshanks’ soft blanket, tucked neatly as he liked it, a perfect little nest of purple wool waiting patiently. The embers cast a soft rosy light, making it look even more inviting.

“Oh, Spindleshanks!” Gib giggled, happy and relieved. “You found it! It was right here all along!” The hedgehog, with a happy wiggle of nose that tickled Gib’s cheek, burrowed into the familiar softness. Gib placed him onto the blanket. Spindleshanks curled into a perfect ball, quills nestled in warm wool, happy and peaceful.

Gib sat beside him. Peace settled like a blanket itself. The little worry had melted like snow in spring sunshine, leaving only the hum of contentment and the quiet joy of being home. Lanterns glowed softly through the ferns. The moon peeked through the trees, shiny moving shapes on the burrow floor. Gib yawned a long sleepy yawn. Spindleshanks was safe, his blanket found, their cozy burrow the warmest most peaceful wonderful place in all the Twinkletop Hills. Gib felt wrapped in the warmest hug in the whole wide world. Soon he closed his moss-green eyes, and they drifted together on the special wool toward dreamland, where sweet dreams bloomed like little flowers. Everything was just right.
